issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award that purports to determine all referred disputes is not incomplete merely because it is silent on a claim for accounts and profits following a declaration that a lease is invalid.
material_facts: The arbitration reference covered disputes concerning a company, its management and the parties’ acts in relation to it.
A claimant sought accounts and a share of profits concerning a company lease.
The award declared the lease invalid and not binding on the company or its shareholders but gave no express direction on the accounting claim.
The award stated that it determined all disputes referred to the arbitrator.
issues.conclusion: The award’s silence on the accounting claim was to be treated as rejection of that relief, not as an omission making the award incomplete.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 30 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, an award may be challenged on the statutory grounds for setting it aside. A court should support an award if reasonably possible; unless the reference specifically requires separate decisions on every claim, an arbitrator may make a consolidated award. Where an award purports to determine all matters referred, the presumption is that it is final and complete, and silence generally amounts to rejection of a claim unless its nature requires specific adjudication. The Court relied on Salby v. Whitbread and Co., Re Brown and the Croydon Canal Co., Jewell v. Christie, and Harrison v. Creswick. An accounting claim did not necessarily follow from invalidating the lease, and an amount due might already have been adjusted in other parts of the award.

rule.if: arbitration_award_challenge and award_professes_to_determine_all_referred_disputes and award_silent_on_accounting_claim and (accounting_not_necessarily_implicit_in_lease_invalidation or accounting_may_have_been_adjusted_elsewhere)

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party challenged an arbitral award on the ground that it did not resolve all referred disputes.
predicates.award_professes_to_determine_all_referre: The award stated that it determined all disputes referred to the arbitrator.
predicates.award_silent_on_accounting_claim: The award did not expressly grant or reject a claim for accounts and profits connected with a lease it invalidated.
predicates.accounting_not_necessarily_implicit_in_l: Invalidating the lease did not necessarily establish that an accounting or payment of profits was due.
predicates.accounting_may_have_been_adjusted_elsewh: The amount potentially due on an accounting might have been taken into account in other provisions of the award.

issues.definition: When an award challenged as incomplete purports to decide all referred disputes and is silent on an accounting claim that does not necessarily follow from the relief granted and may have been adjusted elsewhere, the award is not incomplete.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award is not incomplete merely because it does not prescribe future company management when it sets aside disputed management arrangements and applicable general law governs management.
material_facts: The reference included disputes about the company’s management and expressly mentioned its future management.
The award declared the parties’ disputed management arrangements not binding.
The award did not prescribe a separate arrangement for future management of the company.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a specific provision for future management did not leave a lacuna in the parties’ rights or make the award incomplete; the applicable general law governed management.
issues.legal_principle: An arbitrator need not make a separate provision on every matter unless the reference specifically requires it. When disputed management arrangements are set aside, the general law governing company management may determine the parties’ rights without a further arbitral direction. The Court relied on the applicable provisions of the Indian Companies Act and the general principle that an award should be upheld if reasonably possible.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party challenged an arbitral award on the ground that it did not resolve all referred disputes.
predicates.award_professes_to_determine_all_referre: The award stated that it determined all disputes referred to the arbitrator.
predicates.disputed_management_arrangements_set_asi: The award set aside the disputed arrangements concerning management of the company.
predicates.general_company_law_governs_management: The general law applicable to the company supplies rules governing its management.

issues.definition: When a challenged award purports to decide all referred disputes, sets aside disputed management arrangements, and general company law governs management, the award is not incomplete for lacking a separate management direction.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award that purports to determine all referred disputes is not incomplete merely because it does not expressly address a claim for relief based on alleged misappropriation.
material_facts: A claimant alleged that company money had been misappropriated and sought relief requiring the money to be restored for division among the parties.
Evidence concerning the allegation was presented to the arbitrator.
The award purported to determine all referred disputes but included no specific provision granting relief on the misappropriation claim.
issues.conclusion: The award’s silence on the misappropriation claim meant that the arbitrator had rejected it, so the award was not incomplete on that account.
issues.legal_principle: Where an award professes to determine all matters referred, the presumption is that it disposes finally of them; silence on a claim may therefore signify its rejection. An arbitrator need not separately state a decision on each matter unless the reference specifically requires it. The Court relied on Harrison v. Creswick and the general principles stated in Salby v. Whitbread and Co., Re Brown and the Croydon Canal Co., and Jewell v. Christie.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party challenged an arbitral award on the ground that it did not resolve all referred disputes.
predicates.award_professes_to_determine_all_referre: The award stated that it determined all disputes referred to the arbitrator.
predicates.award_silent_on_misappropriation_claim: The award contained no express provision granting relief on a claim that company money had been misappropriated.

issues.definition: When a challenged award purports to determine all referred disputes and is silent on a misappropriation claim, the award is not incomplete because the claim is treated as rejected.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator does not exceed authority by directing the sale of property to meet costs of filing an award and distributing any surplus among those entitled to the property.
material_facts: The award allocated land to a person to sell it to meet the costs and charges of filing the award and related arbitration materials in court.
The award directed that any remaining proceeds be distributed among persons entitled to share in the property.
The challenge characterized the provision as creating a trust over property that the arbitrator had been asked to divide.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator had merely made provision for filing costs and distribution of surplus proceeds; the objection that the award created an unauthorized trust was based on a misreading and was not maintained.
issues.legal_principle: An award must be read according to what it actually directs. A direction to sell property to meet costs associated with filing the award and to distribute surplus proceeds among those entitled is a provision for costs and distribution, not the creation of an independent trust beyond the arbitrator’s authority.

rule.if: arbitration_award_challenge and award_allocates_property_for_sale and sale_proceeds_cover_award_filing_costs and surplus_proceeds_are_distributed_to_entitled_persons

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party challenged an arbitral award made in a dispute referred to arbitration.
predicates.award_allocates_property_for_sale: The award allocated property to a person for sale.
predicates.sale_proceeds_cover_award_filing_costs: The award directed that sale proceeds be used to meet costs associated with filing the award and related materials.
predicates.surplus_proceeds_are_distributed_to_enti: The award directed that proceeds remaining after those costs be distributed among persons entitled to share in the property.

issues.definition: When a challenged award allocates property for sale to pay award-filing costs and distributes the surplus to those entitled, that direction is within the arbitrator’s authority.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator does not fail to perform the arbitral function by using property valuations agreed to by the parties.
material_facts: The award specified values for items of property and divided the property on that basis.
The proceedings before the arbitrator showed that the parties themselves had agreed to the estimated values used in the award.
The challenge alleged that the arbitrator had failed to value the property independently.
issues.conclusion: Because the values used in the award were those agreed by the parties, the objection that the arbitrator had failed to determine the values had no merit.
issues.legal_principle: Where the parties agree on property values and the award uses those agreed values, the arbitrator’s reliance on them does not establish a failure to perform the arbitral task.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party challenged an arbitral award made in a dispute referred to arbitration.
predicates.award_uses_party_agreed_property_values: The award used property valuations that the parties had agreed before the arbitrator.

issues.definition: When an award challenged in an arbitration uses property values agreed by the parties, that use is not a failure by the arbitrator.
